nodes.note: The square at the top of the town, walk plane 84, 18 by 14: the first thing the party sees is the chapel to one side and the inn across from it, and the main street leaving down the hill. Its program draws its paving, kerbs, its retaining wall and its lanterns. Materials: cobblestone paving with stone-brick kerbs; stone-brick stairs at the flights; retaining walls between terraces of stone bricks with mossy courses at the foot. Light, placed with the place: lanterns on the street's kerb posts at every flight and at every door. The hillside beside the street is the heightmap, stepped turf.

A flight of four stone-brick steps, its own place: six wide and six long, its floor the lower terrace at 80 (the upper street) at its south end, its treads rising to 84 (the square) at its north end; the terrain inside it rises the same way, the ramp its treads climb. Its program draws its treads, its kerb walls and its lanterns. A straight stone wall 32 wide at the water, walk plane 64, with the sea two blocks deep against it (harbour floor 60); the beach lies beyond its western end. The street comes down onto it from the fifth flight; the warehouse's door opens onto it. Materials: stone bricks and polished andesite, with spruce-log bollards along the water edge. Light, placed with the place: lanterns on kerb posts at the flight and at the warehouse door.

A small stone chapel with a short tower, the first thing seen from the square; door east onto the square. Materials (one hand across the town): walls of stone bricks with cobblestone ground floors, spruce timber framing with white (calcite or quartz) infill above; roof of deepslate tiles (slate), with one block of eaves; roof courses chosen against roof-and-facade-craft §2 and §4 (45° stairs over a span W: ceil((W - 1) / 2) courses). Light, placed with the place: a lantern at the door and windows lit from inside. The program draws the whole house, outside and inside; its floor is level with its street and its downhill wall stands on the heightmap's ring.
